subobjective: Describe Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence (Defender TI)
stem: An analyst looks up a domain in Microsoft threat-intel articles. A user clicks a URL in email. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Defender TI detonates mailbox attachments as Safe Attachments
Safe Links is Microsoft's actor encyclopedia
Both jobs are Azure Key Vault certificate issuance
Defender Threat Intelligence provides actor and infrastructure context; Safe Links is the email time-of-click control

explanation: Defender TI is intelligence context. Safe Links is a Defender for Office 365 URL control. Looking up a domain in TI is not the same as protecting mailbox clicks.

source.title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence in Microsoft Defender XDR - Microsoft Defender XDR

subobjective: Describe the privacy principles of Microsoft
stem: Microsoft lists protection of customer data, including security safeguards, among its privacy commitments. Which statement matches that principle?

choices.text: Protecting customer data with security controls is part of Microsoft's privacy commitments, not a reason to ignore encryption or access control
Privacy means Microsoft must disable MFA so support can read mailboxes
Privacy is achieved by publishing NSG allow-all rules
Privacy is a Defender XDR workload name

explanation: Microsoft privacy principles include protection of customer data. Privacy is not a justification for weakening authentication or opening networks.

source.title: General Data Protection Regulation - Microsoft GDPR

subobjective: Describe the privacy principles of Microsoft
stem: A learner says Microsoft's privacy principles and Purview Compliance Manager are the same feature. Which correction is accurate?

choices.text: Privacy principles are a Compliance Manager score formula
Privacy principles are Microsoft's data-handling commitments; Compliance Manager tracks customer improvement actions against assessments
Compliance Manager is Microsoft's public privacy statement
Both are Azure DDoS Protection SKUs

explanation: Privacy principles describe Microsoft's commitments. Compliance Manager is a Purview tool for assessing and improving the customer's control implementation.

source.title: Describe Microsoft’s Service Trust Portal and Privacy Principles

subobjective: Describe the Service Trust Portal offerings
stem: A prospect wants Microsoft's ISO and SOC audit reports. An administrator wants to configure DLP in the tenant. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: The Service Trust Portal is where you create tenant DLP policies
The Purview portal publishes Microsoft's SOC reports as its primary job
Service Trust Portal for Microsoft's audit reports; Microsoft Purview portal for the tenant's DLP configuration
Both jobs are done in Azure Bastion

explanation: STP hosts Microsoft's trust and audit documentation. Tenant compliance configuration is done in Purview. Those portals serve different audiences.

source.title: Compliance offerings for Microsoft 365, Azure, and other Microsoft services.

subobjective: Describe the Microsoft Purview portal
stem: Identity admins work in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Compliance admins need DLP, audit, and eDiscovery. Why is the Entra admin center the wrong primary console for that compliance work?

choices.text: The Entra admin center is the only supported DLP console
eDiscovery holds are Conditional Access grant controls
DLP policies are Azure Bastion settings
Those Purview solutions are reached from the Microsoft Purview portal, not from Entra identity administration

explanation: Entra admin center is for identity. Purview portal is for compliance solutions such as DLP, audit, and eDiscovery.

source.title: Learn about the Microsoft Purview portal

subobjective: Describe Compliance Manager
stem: Compliance Manager shows some GDPR-related actions as Microsoft-managed and others as customer-managed. What does that split mean?

choices.text: Microsoft implements some controls for its service; the customer still completes remaining improvement actions
Customer-managed actions are performed automatically by Azure Firewall
Microsoft-managed actions recertify Entra guest groups
The split means the customer no longer owns any data

explanation: Compliance Manager distinguishes Microsoft-implemented service controls from customer improvement actions. SaaS does not finish the customer's compliance work.

subobjective: Describe the uses and benefits of compliance score
stem: A manager treats compliance score as a pass/fail exam result that proves the company is certified. What is the accurate correction?

choices.text: A score of 100 is Microsoft's official ISO certificate
Compliance score estimates remaining improvement-action progress; it is not itself a certification or exam grade
Compliance score replaces the need for the Service Trust Portal
Compliance score is Defender for Cloud's only secure-score value

explanation: Compliance score is a prioritization metric inside Compliance Manager. It does not certify the organization or replace Microsoft audit reports.

subobjective: Describe the data classification capabilities
stem: Classification found credit-card numbers. A learner says that finding already encrypts the files. What is missing?

choices.text: Sensitive information types automatically issue FIDO2 keys
Classification is Azure DDoS Protection
Classification identifies sensitive items; protection still requires labels, DLP, or other controls that act on those findings
Finding a pattern deletes the file, so encryption is unnecessary

explanation: Classification answers what exists and where. Encryption, labeling, and DLP are separate protection decisions.

subobjective: Describe the benefits of Content explorer and Activity explorer
stem: Content explorer shows where labeled items live. Activity explorer shows labeling, sharing, and DLP events. Why are those explorers not DLP policies?

choices.text: Content explorer blocks outbound credit-card numbers as its primary job
Activity explorer declares records automatically
Both explorers are Azure Firewall application rules
Explorers provide visibility; DLP policies detect and help prevent risky sharing

explanation: The explorers answer where content is and what happened to it. They do not replace DLP prevention policies.

subobjective: Describe sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies
stem: Which two protection outcomes can a sensitivity label apply to a document in addition to classifying it? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Encryption and access restrictions that travel with the file
Visual markings such as headers, footers, or watermarks
Azure DDoS Protection for the author's public IP
Just-in-time Global Administrator activation

explanation: Sensitivity labels can encrypt content and apply markings. They are not DDoS or PIM controls.

subobjective: Describe data loss prevention (DLP)
stem: A file is labeled Confidential and encrypted, but a user can still paste the same credit-card numbers into a Teams chat. Which control is missing?

choices.text: Azure DDoS Protection on the Teams tenant
Data loss prevention policies that detect and restrict sensitive sharing in locations such as Teams
Azure Bastion for the Teams client
Privileged Identity Management eligible roles

explanation: Labels can protect a document. DLP watches sharing channels such as Teams for sensitive information types. Encryption on one file does not automatically DLP the chat channel.

subobjective: Describe data loss prevention (DLP)
stem: Security wants the same credit-card DLP check in Exchange email, SharePoint, Teams, and on endpoints. What should the learner expect?

choices.text: DLP exists only as an Azure NSG application rule
DLP can run only after a file is declared a record
DLP policies can apply across multiple locations rather than only one mailbox
Endpoint DLP is a Conditional Access grant control

explanation: Purview DLP is designed to cover multiple locations including email, sites, chat, and devices. It is not an NSG, a record requirement, or a Conditional Access grant.

subobjective: Describe records management
stem: A records team needs a scheduled review before a declared record can be disposed of at the end of its retention period. Which records-management idea is that?

choices.text: Azure WAF custom rules that delete SharePoint items
Microsoft Entra access reviews of VM start rights
Safe Links time-of-click URL checks
Disposition review, which can require approval before a record is destroyed

explanation: Records management can require disposition review so records are not silently deleted when the retention period ends. WAF, Entra access reviews, and Safe Links are not records disposition.

source.title: Records management for documents and emails in Microsoft 365

subobjective: Describe the uses and benefits of compliance score
stem: Which two elements does Compliance Manager use when it helps an organization understand remaining compliance work? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Improvement actions the customer still needs to complete
A compliance score that estimates progress against recommended controls
Azure DDoS Protection SKU assignment
FIDO2 security-key inventory

explanation: Compliance Manager combines improvement actions and a compliance score to prioritize remaining customer work. DDoS SKUs and FIDO2 inventory are not Compliance Manager elements.

subobjective: Describe insider risk management
stem: DLP blocked a credit-card number in email. Separately, a departing employee downloaded thousands of unlabeled files over two weeks. Which tool is designed for that second pattern?

choices.text: Azure DDoS Protection
Insider Risk Management, which looks for risky user behavior patterns, not only a single DLP match
Azure Bastion
Microsoft Entra Temporary Access Pass

explanation: DLP is policy matching on sensitive content. Insider Risk Management looks at sequences of potentially risky user activity such as departing-employee exfiltration.

subobjective: Describe eDiscovery solutions in Microsoft Purview
stem: Legal needs mailboxes preserved for a lawsuit even if users try to delete messages. How does that differ from a routine retention period?

choices.text: Retention holds are the only way to respond to a lawsuit
eDiscovery hold is a Conditional Access grant control
eDiscovery hold preserves content for a legal matter; retention is a lifecycle keep-or-delete schedule
A lawsuit is preserved only by Azure Firewall

explanation: Legal hold is an eDiscovery preservation action for a matter. Retention policies serve ongoing lifecycle requirements. They can coexist but they are not the same decision.

subobjective: Describe audit solutions in Microsoft Purview
stem: Investigators ask who changed a DLP policy yesterday and from where. They do not need to export an entire mailbox for court. Which Purview capability answers that?

choices.text: Azure Bastion session recording of the mailbox
Microsoft Entra lifecycle workflows
Azure DDoS Protection reports
Audit logging of user and admin activities

explanation: Purview audit records who did what, when, and where. Exporting a mailbox for court is eDiscovery. Bastion, lifecycle workflows, and DDoS reports are not that activity trail.

source.title: Learn about auditing solutions in Microsoft Purview

subobjective: Describe Compliance Manager
stem: A customer must show progress against ISO 27001 improvement actions in their own tenant, not download Microsoft's ISO report. Which tool is that customer-side tracker?

choices.text: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
The Service Trust Portal only
Azure Bastion
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

explanation: Compliance Manager tracks the customer's control implementation. STP publishes Microsoft's evidence. The customer still needs Compliance Manager for their own remaining actions.

subobjective: Describe the benefits of Content explorer and Activity explorer
stem: An investigator knows a file was labeled Highly Confidential this morning and then shared externally. Which explorer shows that activity timeline?

choices.text: Azure DDoS Protection metrics
Activity explorer
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Azure Key Vault insights

explanation: Activity explorer shows labeling, sharing, and DLP-related events. Content explorer would answer where items are stored, not the event timeline.

subobjective: Describe sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies
stem: Users should see Confidential markings on documents, but not every label defined in the tenant. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Every label in the tenant is always visible in Word
Named locations publish sensitivity labels
A label policy publishes selected labels to those users; unused labels can remain unpublished
Network security groups publish labels to Word

explanation: Creating a label does not automatically show it to users. Label policies control publication. This is a different decision from what protection a label applies.

subobjective: Describe retention policies, retention labels, and retention label policies
stem: Email must be kept for seven years, but the same mailbox must still be prevented from sending credit-card numbers. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Retention blocks outbound credit-card numbers as its primary job
DLP is the keep-or-delete lifecycle engine
Both needs are met only by Azure Bastion
Retention keeps content for the required period; DLP prevents risky sharing of sensitive information

explanation: Retention is lifecycle keep-or-delete. DLP is preventive sharing control. A seven-year keep does not by itself stop credit-card exfiltration.

source.title: Learn about retention policies & labels to retain or delete

subobjective: Describe eDiscovery solutions in Microsoft Purview
stem: After a hold is in place, legal still needs to search, review, and export a set of emails for opposing counsel. Which Purview solution family covers that workflow?

choices.text: eDiscovery
Azure DDoS Protection
Microsoft Entra password protection
Azure virtual network peering

explanation: eDiscovery covers hold, search, review, and export for legal matters. DDoS, password protection, and VNet peering do not produce a legal production set.

subobjective: Describe audit solutions in Microsoft Purview
stem: Audit tells who changed a policy. eDiscovery exports mailbox content for a lawsuit. DLP tries to stop a share. Which statement keeps those jobs separate?

choices.text: Audit blocks sharing, eDiscovery is a firewall, and DLP exports mailboxes
Audit is detective history, eDiscovery is legal preservation and production, and DLP is preventive control
All three are Azure Bastion features
All three are Conditional Access grant controls

explanation: SC-900 expects learners to place audit, eDiscovery, and DLP in detective, legal, and preventive roles rather than treating Purview as one interchangeable switch.

source.title: Learn about auditing solutions in Microsoft Purview

subobjective: Describe insider risk management
stem: A manager wants Insider Risk Management to replace Conditional Access and block every risky sign-in. What is the accurate correction?

choices.text: Insider Risk Management is Microsoft's only MFA grant control
Conditional Access is a subset of Insider Risk Management file plans
Insider Risk Management analyzes internal user activity patterns; Conditional Access still evaluates sign-in conditions
Insider Risk Management issues FIDO2 keys

explanation: Insider risk is a Purview compliance capability for internal behavior. Sign-in grants and blocks remain an Entra Conditional Access job.

subobjective: Describe the Microsoft Purview portal
stem: An Azure administrator opens the Azure portal to create a Microsoft Purview DLP policy for Exchange Online and cannot find it. What is the likely reason?

choices.text: DLP policies can be created only in Azure Bastion
Exchange DLP is a network security group
The Azure portal is the only supported Purview console
Microsoft 365 DLP and related Purview solutions are administered in the Microsoft Purview portal, not as an Azure VM setting

explanation: Purview compliance solutions are reached from the Purview portal. The Azure portal is the wrong console for Exchange DLP.

source.title: Learn about the Microsoft Purview portal
